title: Brake Inspections as the Evidence for Warranty Visits
content:
**Standard.** Brake inspections are free at any Crestline store and are the evidence every warranty visit under Brake Service Warranties rests on.

1. *Status at the time of inspection.* The warranty must be in status active when an inspection is recorded against it. The status is read from the company's record of that warranty, the one the inspection is recorded against.
2. *What the technician records.* The technician records the thinnest pad thickness measured and one finding. When the line includes a brake fluid test in every inspection, the fluid is tested on the same visit.
3. *How long an inspection can be used.* A warranty visit may rest only on an inspection no older than the line's inspection validity period, counted in calendar days from the day after the inspection date. The inspection date plus the number of days in the period is therefore the last date on which the inspection can be the basis of a warranty visit.
4. *What is not an inspection.* A thickness the customer measured, or a finding from another shop, is not an inspection.

### What counts as the inspection a warranty visit rests on

| Evidence offered | An inspection? |
|---|---|
| A Crestline technician's inspection recorded against the active warranty, with the thinnest pad and one finding | Yes |
| A pad thickness the customer measured | No |
| A finding from another shop | No |

### Validity on both sides (illustrative period of 10 days)

The period here is illustrative only. For an inspection dated the 3rd of a month, day 1 of the count is the 4th and day 10 is the 13th.

| Date of the warranty visit | Days counted from the day after the inspection | May rest on that inspection? |
|---|---|---|
| 13th | 10 | Yes — no older than the period |
| 14th | 11 | No — older than the period |

### Status on both sides

| Status of the warranty when the inspection is recorded | Inspection may be recorded against it? |
|---|---|
| active | Yes |
| expired, superseded or voided | No — the warranty must be active |
